<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="ניסן_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917950_theRebbe_524" batchId="meluket-_D7_A0_D7_99_D7_A1_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917950_theRebbe_524__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Just as physical dew descends, so too the "dew of Torah" descends and is drawn into the Torah a person learns, with two aspects: the lower aspect drawn through human study and the higher aspect drawn from above, for which human study serves as a vessel, especially in the study of Pnimiyus HaTorah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, just as dew</t>
    <t s="2">(in its simple sense)</t>
    <t s="3">descends and is drawn downward,</t>
    <t s="4">so too is it with the dew of Torah,</t>
    <t s="5">which is drawn and revealed downward in the Torah that a person learns.</t>
    <t s="6">For in addition to the fact that the Holy One, blessed be He, sits and engages in Torah</t>
    <t s="7">(the aspect of the dew of Torah)</t>
    <t s="8">is a granting of power to a person so that he can engage in Torah, and that through his engagement in Torah the Holy One, blessed be He, will read and review opposite him,</t>
    <t s="9">behold, also the matter of the dew of Torah itself is drawn and revealed downward in the Torah that a person learns.</t>
    <t s="10">For in the drawing down of the Torah above into the Torah that a person learns,</t>
    <t s="11">there are two matters.</t>
    <t s="12">The Torah as it is in the Z"T of Atik,</t>
    <t s="13">[is] the rain of Torah.</t>
    <t s="14">And the drawing down of this aspect is through a person's engagement in Torah,</t>
    <t s="15">for since the Z"T of Atik are invested in Arich, the root of the chain of descent,</t>
    <t s="16">therefore a person's engagement in Torah is an arousal from below that awakens and draws down this aspect.</t>
    <t s="17">And the Torah as it is in the G"R of Atik,</t>
    <t s="18">[is] the dew of Torah.</t>
    <t s="19">And the drawing down of this aspect is from above,</t>
    <t s="20">and a person's engagement in Torah is only like a vessel in which the dew of Torah is drawn and revealed.</t>
    <t s="21">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="22">that this—that a person's study of Torah is a vessel for the dew of Torah—is primarily in the study of Pnimiyus HaTorah.</t>
    <t s="23">For since Pnimiyus HaTorah</t>
    <t s="24">(even as it is drawn downward)</t>
    <t s="25">is the Tree of Life, which is above the matter of clarifications,</t>
    <t s="26">therefore it is like a vessel for the essence of Torah, which is above any connection to the chain of descent</t>
    <t s="27">(the G"R of Atik, which are not invested in Arich),</t>
    <t s="28">the dew of Torah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Based on this, the two versions of the Sages' statement—"or Torah" and "tal Torah"—can be explained, where "or Torah" refers to Pnimiyus HaTorah, which serves as a vessel for "tal Torah."</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And based on this, we can explain the connection between the two versions in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory,</t>
    <t s="1">"Whoever uses the light of Torah, the light of Torah revives him,"</t>
    <t s="2">for the version in the Gemara is "light of Torah" and the version in the Yalkut</t>
    <t s="3">is "dew of Torah,"</t>
    <t s="4">and it can be said,</t>
    <t s="5">that "light of Torah" is Pnimiyus HaTorah,</t>
    <t s="6">and the study of Pnimiyus HaTorah is a vessel for the dew of Torah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Similarly in prayer, although generally it is an elevation from below to above, it also contains the aspect of drawing down from above to below, beginning with the verse "Ad-nai, open my lips," which is prayed that one's speech be like Torah, drawing down God's own prayer.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And similarly is it in prayer,</t>
    <t s="2">for although in general it is an elevation from below to above,</t>
    <t s="3">it also contains the matter of drawing down from above to below.</t>
    <t s="4">And the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="5">that the beginning of the prayer of the Silent Amidah</t>
    <t s="6">[which is the main prayer]</t>
    <t s="7">is the verse,</t>
    <t s="8">"Ad-nai, open my lips, and my mouth will declare Your praise,"</t>
    <t s="9">for the recitation of this verse is</t>
    <t s="10">(not only an introduction to prayer,</t>
    <t s="11">but rather)</t>
    <t s="12">the beginning of the prayer itself,</t>
    <t s="13">as it is stated in the Gemara</t>
    <t s="14">that it is like a long prayer.</t>
    <t s="15">And behold, in the Targum on the verse "Ad-nai, open my lips," it is translated,</t>
    <t s="16">"Open my lips in Torah."</t>
    <t s="17">That is,</t>
    <t s="18">that the request in this verse at the beginning of prayer is,</t>
    <t s="19">that the prayer</t>
    <t s="20">(and my mouth will declare Your praise)</t>
    <t s="21">should be like Torah</t>
    <t s="22">("Ad-nai, open my lips in Torah").</t>
    <t s="23">For just as in Torah,</t>
    <t s="24">the Torah that a person learns is the word of G-d,</t>
    <t s="25">"My words that I have placed in your mouth,"</t>
    <t s="26">and the person is like one who responds after the reader,</t>
    <t s="27">so too should the prayer be in the manner of "and my mouth will declare Your praise,"</t>
    <t s="28">that a person's prayer should be</t>
    <t s="29">(not his own prayer,</t>
    <t s="30">but rather)</t>
    <t s="31">that only through it will be drawn down</t>
    <t s="32">("declare" from the term "drawing down")</t>
    <t s="33">"Your praise,"</t>
    <t s="34">the prayer of the Holy One, blessed be He.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
